result.title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints
result.summary: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 LIBERO-Industry 基准，把柔性制造中的产品变体、物料流动、有限执行窗口与几何容差等工业约束转化为可控任务条件，用于评测通用机器人策略（含 VLA 与世界动作模型）。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于机器人操作评测，虽涉及 VLA 策略，但关注任务条件与成功率随约束退化的趋势，未触及内部视觉状态、证据筛选、latent 推理或停止决策机制，缺乏可供 LVR 借鉴的具体线索。
